content.comment_body: Hello, Is there a way within the CPU program to read data unique to a certain [product_name] CPU, like serial number or MAC address? My customer is requesting the open source code, but I would like to restrict duplication of my application to other modules. To achieve this, my program hides a comparison for a specific MAC address and will block functionality if the values do not match. Thank you for your assistance.

Yes, this can be done. For [product_name], it is also possible to use [product_name] software to scan for available network clients. I am not sure how this can be done within the [product_name] program specifically, or how to create an executable file such as EXE, BAT, or VB files.

Hello, In [product_name], you can use memory cards to copy your program. This feature, known as copy protection, requires a compatible memory card for [product_name]. For earlier versions, a specific memory card needs to be ordered from [company_name]. Later versions support standard SD or MicroSD cards. After proper configuration, removing the memory card means the module has no program stored internally. Additionally, you can enable program copy protection. This allows modifications even when copy protection is active. Refer to the relevant manuals for step-by-step instructions.

Thank you for the reply. I need to develop a program. Before the final download, I require reading a value from the PLC that is unique to the specific device and accessible in the PLC program. This value will be inserted into the project and downloaded to the PLC. If the retrieved module value and the stored program value match, the PLC operates as intended. Afterward, I provide the source code to the customer. If they attempt to use the project on another [product_name], the stored value in the project and the new PLC value will be different, leading to certain functions being disabled.
A [product_name] program cannot access the MAC address of a [product_name].
Is there any value that can be read which is unique to a specific CPU?

analysis.insight_summary: The user wants to limit a [product_name] controller program to a specific hardware unit using unique identifiers like MAC address or serial number, in order to prevent unauthorized copying. Other forum members point out that although hardware copy protection by memory card is available, there is no way to access hardware-specific identifiers such as MAC address or serial number directly within the [product_name] programming environment, restricting the ability to implement hardware-bound logic in software.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to access hardware-specific information (e.g., MAC address, serial number) in the [product_name] program for runtime verification, aiming to ensure that the program only functions on the intended hardware device.
